_policy: Every file in python/conduit/tests/test_*.py is either run by bin/run_conduit_tests.py or named here with a `kind`, a reason, an owner, and the thing tracking the debt. There is no third state. Same rule as bin/tests-ci-manifest.json. `kind` decides how an entry is retired: `infrastructure` means the file needs a live PostgreSQL that the hermetic runner deliberately does not provide, so observing a pass on a developer machine (where CONDUIT_PG_DSN happens to be exported) is NOT evidence the debt is closed — these are retired by landing the DB-tier job named in `clears_when`, not by a green run; `structural` means the file is not a test (shared helper) or is a superseded stub, and it is retired by deleting it or populating it. Exclusions may only shrink: the runner fails with exit 2 if a named file no longer exists.
_why_this_exists: At origin/main 00a28c5b no CI workflow ran python/conduit/tests at all — the Python conduit suite was gated by nothing, so it passed or failed only on whatever machine ran it by hand. Building this gate immediately found a guard that had been failing on main unnoticed: tests/test_c2_validate_receipt.py::test_unblock_plan_has_validation matched the first `unblock_plan:` occurrence in tools.ts, which is a line inside a comment, and had been asserting against prose since it was written (fixed in the same commit as this manifest). The runner scrubs PYTHONPATH and CONDUIT_PG_DSN so a test cannot pass by borrowing the developer's database; that is what makes the 13 infrastructure entries below visible instead of silently green.

test_helpers.py.reason: Shared helper module, not a test file: it provides create_test_schema / drop_test_schema / cleanup_orphaned_test_schemas / TestSchema, and other tests import it as `tests.test_helpers`. It is matched by the test_*.py discovery glob, so it is named here explicitly rather than renamed (renaming would break `from tests.test_helpers import ...` across the suite).
test_helpers.py.clears_when: n/a by design — this is the one permanent entry; it stops being an exclusion only if the module is renamed AND every importer updated in the same change
